source.title: Factual Retrieval in LLMs Is a Redundant, Distributed and Non-Contiguous Process
source.authors: Hail Hochman; Natalie Shapira; Yoav Goldberg

page_placements.theme: Redundant parallel pathways rather than active compensation: removing one component, edge or layer changes little, removing several together changes much

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses hydra effects and reports on redundant factual-computation paths, but it does not test whether ablating a component triggers downstream compensation or reduces the ablation’s total effect.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior hydra-effect and backup-head results, which are not rows. Its own patching experiments identify alternative factual-retrieval paths; these measure structural path redundancy, not self-repair after component ablation. The few-shot prompt instructions in the appendix are addressed to a classifier, not to an AI reading or reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: The study searches for alternative minimal layer paths via counterfactual patching of entity-token activations in LLaMA 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B. It never ablates a layer, head or MLP in an otherwise normal forward pass and measures how much downstream components restore the output. Its 'backup paths' are found by forcing the search past the primary path, and the authors state it is unclear whether these paths are used in unperturbed runs. That is structural redundancy under heavy intervention, a related but different construct from self-repair. Hydra effect and backup heads appear only as cited prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that factual attribute computation is multi-step, sparse and non-contiguous, and that it is redundant, with multiple functionally equivalent paths. They frame this as knowledge being distributed, possibly explaining the localization-editing mismatch. They do not claim to show ablation-triggered self-repair, and they note the deeper paths may not be used in unperturbed passes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses iterative activation patching and counterfactual entity activations to identify minimal and alternative factual-retrieval paths; it does not ablate an attention component and measure downstream output repair.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported depth of alternative-path computation changes with counterfactual noise: in the locked/noise-free setting, alternative paths terminate deeper on average than under the original isolate operation.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-identical alternative minimal attribute paths were found in 80.1% (LLaMA) and 82.7% (Qwen) of CounterFact prompts. These paths are deeper and longer than the primary paths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Factual attribute computation at the entity token admits multiple functionally equivalent layer paths, accessible under intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Hybrid primary-prefix/alternative-suffix paths succeed for 35.4% (LLaMA) and 32.8% (Qwen) of prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer roles across redundant factual-recall paths are partly interchangeable.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper states that its greedy search may miss valid paths and that its redundancy estimate is a lower bound. It also says it is unclear whether the deeper paths are used in unperturbed forward passes or are degenerate remnants of training. No results directly test ablation-induced self-repair.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant self-repair or ablation results were reported. Other path-structure statistics and functional analyses were not extracted because they do not measure ablation-induced compensation.

untested.parts: Layer ablation followed by measured downstream attention-layer compensation of the output.
Late-MLP erasure of the top token and its reduction after upstream ablation.
Single-head ablation on general text across families and sizes.
Distribution of compensation fraction, per-prompt variance, overcorrection.
Backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling, anti-erasure neurons.
Self-repair under mean or resample versus zero ablation.
Whether ablation importance misstates component function because of compensation. The paper's editing-localization remark is speculative and not tied to self-repair.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's gate judgment holds. 'Backup paths' are named by analogy to McGrath et al. and Wang et al., but no ablation-compensation quantity is measured. The noise-free variant shifts alternative-path depth deeper (LLaMA 17.73 vs 13.93), which indicates the redundancy findings depend on the intervention method.

versions.untested_parts: Whether ablating an attention layer causes later attention layers to compensate and restore the output.
Late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token and its change after earlier-component ablation.
Head ablation, full-distribution compensation on general text, and comparison across model families and sizes.
Prompt-level variation and overcorrection in self-repair after ablation.
Whether the named mechanisms carry self-repair following ablation.
Whether self-repair occurs under mean or resample ablations.
Whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function because of self-repair.

relation.reason: Section 2 discusses the Hydra effect and backup heads, relating them to factual-retrieval redundancy without testing downstream compensation.

tranche.reason: The experiments identify redundant factual-retrieval paths through activation patching; they neither measure ablation-triggered self-repair nor use self-repair as a tool.

source_check.notes: R3 and R4 are descriptive path-length statistics, including the embedding layer, rather than main self-repair outcomes. The limitations explicitly leave unclear whether deeper alternative paths operate during unperturbed forward passes.
